Player moved LEFT from (2, 2) to (2, 0). So LEFT works but RIGHT doesn't from (2, 2). This is very strange.
Wait, let me reconsider. Maybe the player CAN move RIGHT from (2, 2), but something is blocking. Let me check the animation of the failed RIGHT action.
Actually, let me think about this differently. What if the player moves 1 cell at a time, not 2? Let me check:
- From (4, 0), UP moved to (2, 0) = 2 cells up. 
- From (2, 0), RIGHT moved to (2, 2) = 2 cells right.
- From (2, 2), RIGHT didn't move.
- From (2, 2), LEFT moved to (2, 0) = 2 cells left.
So the player moves 2 cells per action when possible. But RIGHT from (2, 2) didn't work. Why?
Let me check: maybe the player can only move to cells that have a clear path. From (2, 2) to (2, 4), the path goes through (2, 3) which is 'g'. From (2, 0) to (2, 2), the path goes through (2, 1) which is also 'g'. Both are the same, so this shouldn't matter.
Wait, maybe the issue is that the player is blocked by the red block's "influence"? The red block is at (2, 8), which is 4 cells away from (2, 2). That seems too far.
Or maybe the player can only move to cells that are the same color as the starting cell. The player started at (4, 0) which is 'b' (blue, the player's starting color). The player moved to (2, 0) which is 'W'. Then from (2, 0) to (2, 2) which is also 'W'. But from (2, 2) to (2, 4), the destination is 'W' as well. So this shouldn't matter.
Let me try RIGHT again from (2, 0) to see if the player can move to (2, 2) again.
Actually wait, I just realized something. When I tried RIGHT from (2, 2) and it didn't work, the step stayed at 27. But when I tried LEFT from (2, 2) and it worked, the step went to 28. So the RIGHT action was indeed a no-op.
But why? Let me check the animation of the RIGHT action to see if the player tried to move but was blocked.
Actually, let me try a different approach. Let me try RIGHT from (2, 0) and see if the player moves to (2, 2). If it does, then the issue is specific to being at (2, 2). If it doesn't, then there's a global issue with RIGHT.
